brief: A planter for a sunny kitchen windowsill with three herbs growing in it.

requirements.requirement: Planter suitable for sunny kitchen windowsill
requirements.evidence: Build is a compact 3-cell linear planter 334x89x335mm with open-top full-depth bins suitable for windowsill placement; sunny exposure, material UV/heat resistance and waterproofing cannot be verified by configurator and depends on user-chosen print material.

Three bins each filled with soil to rim and planted: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full with basil-young, bin:1,-1,0~hex-bin-full with mint-young, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full with parsley-young - all visible in build and check_build shows no PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL warnings.

finish.summary: Three-cell windowsill planter built from pieces at (0,0), (1,0), (1,-1) each with full-depth bin filled with soil and planted with basil, mint and parsley. Joints locked, meshClash clear, suitable compact size for kitchen windowsill.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text:
A sunny kitchen windowsill planter with three herbs growing in it.

**Build:** 3-cell linear cluster (334 x 335 mm footprint, 89mm tall parts, 163mm to herb tops) — compact size suitable for windowsill. Three adjacent full-depth bins (`bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full`, `bin:1,-1,0~hex-bin-full`, `bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full`) each filled to rim with soil and planted:
- Basil young in left cell
- Mint young in middle cell  
- Parsley young in right cell

All bins locked with jointBolts, meshClash clear, no prop warnings.

Sunny/drainage/material claims are not verifiable by configurator (requires user choice of material) — shape provides open-top planter function.
